newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul central bank to cut bank reserve rate - report.
newsitem.headline: Seoul central bank to cut bank reserve rate - report.

text.p: The Bank of Korea plans to cut the bank reserve requirement rate by two percentage points to an average of 3.5 percent during the first half of this year, the Dong-A Ilbo newspaper quoted the bank governor as saying on Friday.

"(The bank) plans to lower the bank reserve requirement rate by two percentage points to an average of 3.5 percent from the current 5.5 percent," Lee Kyung-shick was quoted as saying in an interview with the newspaper.
To absorb surplus liquidity from the cut, the central bank plans to reduce the bank's rediscount lending to commercial banks, the report said.
Lee was also quoted as saying he expected the lowered reserve rate to increase liquidity by about 2.5 trillion won.
The reserve rate is the proportion of deposits that banks must place as reserves with the central bank.
The South Korean central bank lowered the rate to an average of 5.5 percent on November 8 from 7.4 percent.
The lower reserve rate is expected to be swiftly followed cuts in bank lending rates, now at around 12 percent.
He was also quoted as saying the nation's interest rates could drop by a percentage point every year over the next five years.
President Kim Young-sam said on Tuesday a panel would be set up to oversee restructuring of the local financial industry.
There has been speculation that his remarks would be followed by a cut in the reserve rate.
Central bank officials could not immediately be reached for comment. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727-5646
